1
Heritage & Storytelling
Audemars Piguet exemplifies a 
bold identity in the watch 
world. Since the brand is the 
oldest luxury Swiss 
watchmaking manufacturer 
still owned and operated by its 
founding families, they 
continue to ignore trends and 
develop timeless pieces. 
2
Stylistic Identity
Audemars Piguet focuses on 
unique styles that differ from 
other luxury watches. For 
instance their stainless steel 
watch being a key part of their 
collection and priced higher 
than gold pieces sets them 
apart. This attracts clients that 
differ drastically from 
competitors style of 
watchmaking. 
3
Retail Identity
4
Audemars Piguet’s retail 
experience is defined by their 
luxe, minimalist interior design 
that feels conversational and 
almost homey. The retail 
experience is said to feel like 
entering a luxurious private 
residence, noting a sort of 
intimacy when entering. 
Communication Identity
Audemars Piguet’s 
communication is sophisticated, 
deeply rooted in storytelling to 
create one of a kind purchases. 
The timeless tone emphasizes 
their exclusivity, high class 
branding, and heritage of their 
watches. 
Audemars Piguet
Carson and Grace
Brand Identity
Timeless watches, excellent craftsmanship

Market Analysis 
Founded in 1875, Jules Louis Audemars 
and Edward Auguste Piguet combined 
their expertise to construct the brand 
Audemars Piguet.
-
Family owned business
-
Prioritizing quality and exclusivity over 
trends or exposure
-
Sourced internally, building scarcity
-
Established itself among the "Holy Trinity" 
of watchmaking brands, making it among 
the most luxurious and prestigious globally
-
However, it is generally considered part of 
an ultra-luxury tier alongside Patek Philippe 
and Richard Mille.
Audemars Piguet
Carson and Grace

Audemars Piguet
Carson and Grace
The brand quickly became influential in the 
watchmaking business, creating the first
-
“Minute repeater wristwatch” (1892) 
-
The Royal Oak (1972), and launched 
their first luxury steel sports watch
-
Watches for women 
AP produces 50,000 watches a year
Patek - 65,000 per year
Rolex - 1.2 million per year

~$25,000 – $40,000
Mid-range: 
~$40,000 – $100,000
High complications:

-
Gold (rose, yellow, white)
-
Platinum
-
Ceramic & forged carbon
-
Gems/ diamonds 
    Product Positioning
-
Ultra-luxury Swiss watchmaker
-
Emphasis on craftsmanship & 
heritage
-
Low production, high exclusivity
-
Strong design identity (iconic 
shape and color scheme)
Audemars Piguet
Carson and Grace

Gen Z
Who is Gen Z?
-
DOB ranges from 1997–2012 
-
Currently accounts for approximately 20% 
of global personal luxury goods
-
Highly influenced by growing social media 
platforms and peers
Characteristics and Preferences 
-
Technology based mindset: discovery online through 
social media platforms
-
Individual expression: purchases tend to reflect beliefs 
over status 
-
Environmentally aware: prioritize sustainability and 
ethics 
-
Financially conscious: more cautious/ less impulsive ( 
research w/ technology)
-
Prefer Transparency

Gen Z Trends 
Vintage shopping 
-
Strong interest in pre-owned luxury 
(40% considering second-hand 
watches)
Customization 
-
Gen Z wants unique, tailored products
Mixing wardrobe 
-
Combines luxury with vintage and 
streetwear
-
Focus on style over brand name

Pricing & Distribution
●
Prices can range from $10,000 - $400,000+
○
Price on request system 
●
Only produces 50,000 a year
○
Leads to scarcity to build luxury
●
Most of the time customers have to wait to 
buy an AP watch
Communication Strategy
●
Collaborations are labeled as “friends of the 
brand”
○
Don’t give out gifts
●
Social media and website “savvy”
○
Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Youtube

product, but for people”

●
Built on heritage, craftsmanship,

Geared towards a “young” approach
●
Family stands for four pillars
○
Music, art, sport, gastronomy
●
Emphasis on exclusivity
Offer System
●
Always let the client make the choice
○
“Know your client”
○
Emphasis on the numbers 
○
Key CRM

Recommendations
Targeting
●
When targeting Gen Z, make sure to 
target the later half of the age 
category
○
More disposable income and out 
of college (21 to 29)
●
Focus on the segment of Gen Z that 
identities as “entrepreneurs”
Communication
●
Leverage the luxury feel that the 
production scarcity has
○
Gen Z who can afford an AP like 
to brand about it
Marketing and Communication 
●
Utilize more UGC
○
Utilizing friends of the brand that speak to 
Gen Z (or a friend of a brand that is Gen Z)
●
Promoting AP x Music to Gen Z 
○
Gen Z is very connected to music artists
■

an artist or music video to buy a 
specific item of clothing”

Potential Collaboration
●
8/10 of Gen Z globally are 
looking to improve their general 
well-being
●
Oura’s stake in the Gen Z 
market
○
Gen Z women are Oura’s 
fastest growing segment 
as of 2025 
●
Directly aligning with Gen Z’s 
desires without compromising 
brand identity could be crucial 
for solidifying this target 
audience while utilizing Oura’s 
popularity within the segment
Audemars Piguet
Carson and Grace
X
Why for Gen Z?
The perfect combination of luxury 
meets well-being. This collaboration is 
a play on Audemars Piguet’s luxury 
design with Oura’s sleek tracking 
system, allowing users to reach their 
health goals discreetly. 
These AP watches will have Oura’s 
health tracking technology inside of 
the watch, but not change the design 
of the watch at all, maintaining AP’s 
branding and identity.
